standout_why: Compared against the cited SoundGuys 'best noise cancelling headphones' guide (read 2026-11-08): it lists list prices only (Sony $449.99/$459.99, Bose $449/$449.99, AirPods Max 2 $549, HDB 630 $499.95, Momentum 5 $399.95, JBL Tour One M3 $399.95/$449.95, Sonos Ace Ultra $449, Beats 360 $349, Bose QC Headphones 2nd Gen $359, Nothing Headphone (a) $199, Soundcore Space 2 $129.99) with no maker-store date and no numeric ANC measurement; ChatGPT's own cards already carry retailer prices for its four picks ($378 Walmart Sony, $369 B&H Bose, $449 Walmart AirPods Max 2, $299.95 Nordstrom Momentum 4), so the Bose $369 figure is confirmed rather than new, and the AirPods Max 2 card price ($449) is $100 under Apple's own $549. The two What Hi-Fi pages ChatGPT cited could not be read (WebFetch returned only the title; raw downloads were blocked by the sandbox). What is new: maker-direct prices with dates for the whole ladder, the Sennheiser-refurbished Momentum 4 at $199.95, Bose's own footnote that its tested battery is 24 h (18 h with Immersive Audio) rather than the 30 h headline ChatGPT repeated, and the priced sub-$200 tier.
decides: Confirms the Sony-vs-Bose split ChatGPT gave: at the maker, Bose is $369 today while Sony's own XM6 price could not be opened (Sony blocked both sony.com hosts), so the only sourced flagship discount is Bose's $80 off. It moves the 'value' pick: ChatGPT's cheapest option was the Momentum 4 at $299.95, but Sennheiser itself sells a refurbished Momentum 4 for $199.95 and Soundcore's Space One ($99.99) and Space 2 ($129.99) claim 40 h and 50 h of ANC playback, 10 to 20 h more than the Sony and Bose headline figures, at a quarter of the price. AirPods Max 2 loses on price at the maker ($549, 20 h) by a wider margin than ChatGPT's $449 card implied.
